correctness.rationale: Assari--Hosseinzadeh--Macpherson's finite-set analysis yields convex equivalence classes around an odd balanced quotient with dihedral induced symmetry; the cyclic class-size sequence up to rotation/reversal determines the finite type. Every odd cyclic composition is realizable by clustering dense-circle points near a balanced odd-gon skeleton. Block-start encoding gives precisely odd-weight bracelets. Burnside's lemma yields the rotation and reflection terms. Babai--Cameron's local-order formula then gives the self-converse count after quotienting by converse. The assigned verifier brute-forces bracelets through length 14 and checks the formulas through length 20.

value.rationale: Finite-set orbit growth is a central oligomorphic invariant of \(N_3\). The exact all-arity formula, asymptotic, and self-converse local-order count substantially sharpen the exponential-scale information motivating the source literature.

final_claim: For the set-homogeneous hypergraph \(N_3\), the automorphism-group orbits on \(k\)-element subsets are exactly odd-weight binary bracelets of length \(k\), giving the stated Burnside formula, asymptotic \(2^{k-2}/k+O(2^{k/2})\), and self-converse local-order count \(2^{\lfloor(k-1)/2\rfloor}\).
limitations: Unordered finite subsets, not ordered tuples.
